title: A 3nm FinFET 2.2Gsearch/s 0.305fJ/b TCAM with Dynamically Gated Search Lines for Data-Center ASICs
problem: Ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM) for packet classification in data-center networks consumes excessive power due to parallel all-entry search, impacting operational efficiency and environmental footprint of network devices.
motivation: Data-center network switches require fast parallel TCAM lookups for packet classification and forwarding, but power consumption is a critical bottleneck limiting deployment scale and reliability.
method: This 3nm FinFET design reduces power in TCAM (ternary content-addressable memory—a device that searches memory entries against patterns) by using dynamically gated search lines, which selectively activate only the entries that need searching rather than all entries at once. Asymmetric-split architecture further reduces power by adjusting consumption based on the number of bits being searched. Together they achieve 37.4% power savings and 46.6% lower peak current.
key_novelty: Dynamically gating search lines—turning them on selectively to search only the needed entries instead of searching all at once—reduces power consumption in TCAM.
limitations: Abstract-only; area overhead, latency impact, search accuracy/false positives, and datacenter deployment results not discussed.
primary_theme: Low-power gated-search TCAM for data-center networking
